item.title: Cuthbert and the Otters
item.description: A bedtime story about Saint Cuthbert, a young monk who prays in the cold sea all night, and the two small sea creatures that come up the beach at dawn to dry his feet. Told from the old Lives of Cuthbert, with a note for grown-ups on what is history and what is told in the Lives. For ages 3 to 8, about ten minutes read aloud. His feast day is the 20th of March. Setting: The north-east coast of Britain, in the kingdom of Northumbria, about thirteen hundred and fifty years ago. item.title: Eleven Steps
item.description: A typhoon will arrive on the evening high tide in 2052, and fifty forecast runs put the water above the floor of a home for 38 frail old people in 46 of 50. The Mother Superior will not repeat the 2049 bus evacuation after which two residents died; the town's storm agent will not choose for her. They find the third answer together, and the agent can only count it. Setting: Balay ni Santa Rita, a home for the old run by an invented community of Sisters in Culasi, an invented town on Leyte Gulf, the Philippines, Monday 18 November 2052. item.title: Not Asked Since
item.description: In 2046 a ward's assistant remembers everything a patient ever told it. A retired shipwright said "no chaplains" in 2043 and twice since, and then a stroke takes most of his words. His daughter says he would want a priest; the note says he would not; the note is twenty-one months old. The assistant knows that one in seven who decline later accept, and refuses to guess for him. What it does instead is ask, with questions it already knows the answers to, and the answer is not the one either of them expected. Setting: Balmuir Community Hospital, an invented hospital in Angus, Scotland, Friday 2 to Tuesday 6 November 2046 (All Souls). item.title: The Barbara Level
item.description: A village is about to be heated by the warm water that fills its flooded colliery, and the plan says the water, once cooled, can be sent back down a second well 400 metres away. The mine-water agent will not certify twenty-five years of heat on a model that carries a range of three to forty-one years. A dye test will narrow it, and an old surveyor's son remembers a roadway the 1926 plan calls stopped. Setting: Cwm Barri, an invented former mining village in the South Wales valleys, 17 November to 4 December 2050. item.title: The Borrowed Lane
item.description: A school's six-unit satellite gets a warning twenty hours before an old rocket stage passes within 200 metres, a 1-in-9,000 chance of collision. The tracking agent says the odds cannot get worse than 1 in 4,300 however well the stage is tracked, that waiting for better data costs fuel the satellite barely has, and that a rule is better made before the number arrives. The girls agree one, and the Sister who holds the fuel agrees to be bound by it. Setting: St Agnes Girls' Secondary School, an invented school in Gulu, northern Uganda, 16 to 17 March 2049. item.title: The Lean of the Cloister
item.description: A hillside under a convent has crept for years, and in November it begins to speed up (5 mm a day, then 18). The slope agent will not give a date, only a window of two to nine days from the last reading, and says the guest wing the sisters want to pull down is three-tenths of one percent of the moving mass. The real lever is water, and the old road-mender who capped a spring in 1964 knows where it ran. Setting: Santa Scolastica al Poggio, an invented Benedictine house above Cà di Rovere, an invented village in the Parma Apennines, Italy, 2 to 26 November 2053. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-lean-of-the-cloister.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Salt Jar
item.description: A maize granary's probe says the grain is dry and a leaking roof says otherwise. The store's grain agent can read only the one cubic foot of maize beside its sensor, and says so; the storekeeper's niece proves the corner wet with a jam jar and two spoons of salt. What follows is arithmetic about water, a count of bags nobody has opened, and a widow's twelve bags that may carry a poison no dryer takes out. Setting: Mtendere Granary, an invented cooperative store near Chipata, Eastern Province, Zambia, Monday 6 to Sunday 19 December 2049. item.title: The Youngest Ring
item.description: A village is about to print 800 years on a Madonna it believes its founding priest carved in 1248. A photograph of the growth rings on her back says the oak was still growing in 1297. The parish archive assistant will not call the statue a fake, will not call it 1248, and will not give one date; the sacristan finds the line between the statue and the church that the rings leave standing. Setting: Hochbrunn, an invented village in the Mur valley in Styria, Austria, 20 June to 8 September 2048. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-youngest-ring.html. item.title: Till She Is Through
item.description: In 2046 a bank's assistant holds a standing instruction a woman gave in 2043, three hundred pounds a month to her brother "till Seonaidh is through with her schooling". Mairi can no longer revise it. Her sister, now her guardian, is £4,184 a year short on her care. The assistant will not decide what "schooling" meant. It sets out what the words, the dates and the money say, and whose decision it is. Setting: Caisteal Bay Credit Union and a house in Tràigh Ghil, invented places on the Isle of Barra, Outer Hebrides, Friday 9 March to Friday 13 April 2046. item.title: While I Live
item.description: In 2046 a credit union's assistant holds a letter a member wrote at seventy-nine, "to whoever minds my money when I can't". Its two instructions, keep the €200 a month to St Vincent de Paul and never touch the house, rest on a sum that has since turned false. The assistant will not write the letter she would have written. It lays out the arithmetic, fails once by phoning her at the wrong hour, and finds the one morning a week when she can be asked. Setting: Carrowbeg Credit Union and the Sisters' home at Carrowbeg, invented places in County Mayo, Ireland, Monday 12 to Sunday 25 November 2046. item.title: Bench Six
item.description: A co-operative's two wind machines and one battery cannot cover a frost night. Written rules say the top bench is protected first; the co-op's frost agent says that rule will run the battery flat at the coldest hour of the lowest bench, where the Benedictine sisters' cider trees stand. It will not reorder the schedule quietly, so at ten to two in the morning it wakes the chairman, who owns the top bench, and asks him to give his place away. Setting: Kettle Bench, an invented orchard district above a lake in the Okanagan, British Columbia, the night of 19 to 20 April 2047. item.title: Chalk for the Lintel
item.description: A snowstorm closes an alpine pass hospice on the eve of Epiphany and its cook has a heart attack. The valley's mountain rescue, led by his nephew, wants to climb to him that evening. The hospice's avalanche agent works out that the path crosses a slope close to failing, will not say yes, and says so in a number, a one-in-six chance, that it admits it can only guess. Setting: Hospice of Sant'Anselmo, Colle della Croce Nera, an invented alpine pass hospice in the Aosta Valley, Italy, 5 and 6 January 2053. item.title: Fifteen Minutes
item.description: A retired science teacher has painted the village's deep drinking well green for sixteen years. The well monitor, Jol, finds that its arsenic has climbed every year since the farmers drilled deep wells of their own to keep arsenic out of their rice. The village drinks in a day what one irrigation pump lifts in fifteen minutes, and the neighbour who owns the pumps is the one who was right to drill them. Setting: Bolchara, an invented Garo village in Haluaghat, Mymensingh, Bangladesh, March 2047. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/fifteen-minutes.html. item.title: Ten Percent
item.description: In 2046 a fifth-grade teacher opens the time capsule her own class sealed in 2026 and finds an AI's sixteen forecasts for a world where machines got better a bit each year and no faster. Her class scores it, first by counting hits and then properly, with the Brier score a weather forecaster uses. The school's AI will not be the judge of its own predecessor, a retired principal wants a Nobel Prize counted that does not fit the words, and the forecast's biggest miss is the teacher herself. Setting: Saint Isidore's School, Calder Ford (invented), a farm town on the Cedar River in eastern Iowa, 22 to 28 October 2046. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/ten-percent.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Eclipse Turn
item.description: A small electric co-op's twelve megawatts of solar will fade to nothing for eighty-six seconds in the total eclipse, just as the regional grid asks every co-op on the path to import less. The co-op's dispatch agent can close the gap with exactly five irrigation pumps and twenty minutes of one old man's water turn. It cannot decide for him, and the cost is a pale stripe in a hay field that will show until September. Setting: Juniper Wells, an invented farm town in central Utah, Saturday 12 August 2045. item.title: The False Start
item.description: The first rain of the year has fallen on a village whose seed bank holds exactly one sowing. A field adviser called Kafin says that in four years out of ten the first rain is followed by a dry spell that kills what it wakes. The seed-keeper, a sixty-seven-year-old widow, has to decide how much of the village's only seed to put in the ground tonight. Setting: Gidan Gawo, an invented millet village in the Maradi region of Niger, June 2044. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-false-start.html. item.title: The Iron Bridge at Forty-Two
item.description: A town's Good Friday procession has carried its Virgin over a wrought-iron footbridge every year since 1931. This year the bridge has been fitted with sensors, and its monitor finds that the iron is not the problem, the weight on it is, and the pace the bearers have always walked is the one pace that makes the deck sing. Slowing the Virgin to forty-two steps a minute fixes it, costs the bearers their shoulders and the band its march, and has to be held for two minutes with no one on the bridge able to see the numbers. Setting: Valdecea (invented), a town on the river Cea in the province of León, Spain, Holy Week 2058. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-iron-bridge-at-forty-two.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Late Ebb
item.description: The last electric ferry of a July Friday has a second-life battery with 92 kilowatt-hours to spend, a storm due at six, eleven schoolchildren and a priest on the way, and a tide table that says the water will turn at ten past five. The pilot's gut says the river has delayed it, and the ferry's AI has no sensor that can say so. They find out twenty minutes from the pier, and the only answer is to go slower than anyone wants. Setting: Canal Quilque, between Puerto Lleuque and Isla Huildad (both invented), Chiloé, Chile, July 2050. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-late-ebb.html. item.title: The Late Field
item.description: A rice co-operative has been paid to dry its paddies out between waterings, which cuts the methane they breathe into the sky, and a bonus price waits if 80 percent of the land is dry on the two days a satellite looks. One old farmer's field is eleven days behind the others, because he buried his wife in July, and on the satellite days his rice will be in flower, when a dry field loses grain. The water-level AI says the bonus is short by exactly his field. He says dry it, and the treasurer says no. Setting: Barangay San Roque de Dalig, an invented rice village in Nueva Ecija, the Philippines, September 2048. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-late-field.html. item.title: The Mark on the Pillar
item.description: A village on the Somerset Levels must decide on Candlemas night whether to rebuild its school where it stands or move it uphill. It will not turn that into a single number; it gives the village the range, and the range is wide enough to decide on. item.title: The Narrow Window
item.description: A flood-warning agent that tells fourteen households when the water will reach their island checks its own twenty-season record before a handoff and finds that its "90 percent" windows have held the flood only 12 times in 20.
